confirmed.title: Snapshots and tracked summaries include stale reports from earlier runs (wrong numbers under new tags)
confirmed.scenario: snapshot() copies every file in docs/reports, including outputs that the current run never produced: skipped steps (ablation_ann, locomo_ann, retention), steps that failed this time, and old logs. report.collect() then folds them into summary.json, and that becomes evaluation/reports/<tag>_summary.json. I checked the existing snapshots. The e2 and e4 MANIFEST step lists have no ablation_test_ann or locomo_ann. Yet docs/reports/e2/ablation_ann/results.json and docs/reports/e4/ablation_ann/results.json are the baseline file (created_at 2026-10-12T01:15, pool 20, structure None, pre-fix LSH with Recall@5 0.32 against 0.90 exact), and e2_summary.json and e4_summary.json carry them as sections. Running `report_delta.py baseline e4` therefore shows ANN and locomo_ann deltas of exactly 0 and implies the LSH fix changed nothing. A step that fails also leaves its previous output in place, presented as current.
confirmed.fix: Before running each planned step, delete or move its output files. Snapshot only files written during this run (keep an explicit output list per step, or require mtime >= run start). Record any intentionally reused report, such as retention under --skip-retention, in MANIFEST as reused_from: <tag/created_at>. Have report.collect drop or flag any section whose created_at is older than the run start.

verdict.evidence:
I checked this end to end by reading the code and the files already on disk. I did not edit the repo or run any measurement.

1. Snapshot copies everything. In scripts/measure_all.py lines 75-79, snapshot() copies every entry in docs/reports/ except tag directories that hold a MANIFEST.json. No step deletes its output before it runs, and nothing filters by mtime or by the outputs a step is expected to produce. Lines 87-92 then copy docs/reports/summary.json to the tracked evaluation/reports/<tag>_summary.json. That copy keeps only tag, created_at, git_head, dirty_tree and dataset_sha256 from the manifest and drops the 'steps' list. So the tracked file cannot show which steps actually ran or which ones failed.

2. The summary reads whatever files exist. evaluation/report.py collect() (lines 120-160) loads ablation_ann/results.json and locomo_retrieval_ann.json if they are present. It never checks created_at or the protocol. The report step therefore turns stale files into the summary sections.

3. The existing snapshots show the problem.
   - Steps in each MANIFEST:
     - baseline (2026-10-12T01:28): includes ablation_test_ann and locomo_ann.
     - e2 (15:45): build_dataset, ablation_test, ablation_dev, locomo, classification, lifecycle, report. No ANN steps.
     - e4 (16:17): the same list as e2. No ANN steps.
   - Even so, docs/reports/{baseline,e2,e4}/ablation_ann/results.json are byte-identical (sha1 dcc1e922...). Each has created_at 2026-10-12T01:15:01, candidate_limit 20 and ann true.
   - locomo_retrieval_ann.json is also identical in all three (sha1 9525ba15...).
   - evaluation/reports/e2_summary.json and e4_summary.json both have an 'ablation_ann' section and a 'locomo_retrieval_ann' section. ablation_ann vector recall_at_5 is 0.3185 in both, the baseline value.
   - docs/reports/e4/SUMMARY.md has a section titled "LoCoMo evidence retrieval (approximate search)" with no note that it is stale.

4. Running `scripts/report_delta.py baseline e4 --match ablation_ann.vector.` prints +0.0000 for every metric, and `--match locomo_retrieval_ann` does the same. That implies the LSH rewrite changed nothing.

5. The same path hits a failed step. A non-zero exit leaves the previous output in docs/reports. That output is snapshotted and summarized as if current, and the failure is recorded only in the untracked MANIFEST.

The one intentional reuse is retention under --skip-retention. Even that is never recorded as reused anywhere.
verdict.fix:
In measure_all.py, give each step an explicit output list, for example ablation_test -> docs/reports/ablation, ablation_test_ann -> docs/reports/ablation_ann, locomo_ann -> docs/reports/locomo_retrieval_ann.json, and report -> summary.json/SUMMARY.md.

- Before running the plan, delete (or move into an archive dir) the outputs of every step that is not in the plan, plus summary.json and SUMMARY.md. The only exception is longmemeval_retention.json when --skip-retention is set.
- Before each planned step runs, delete that step's own outputs so a failed step leaves nothing behind.
- Record each intentionally reused report in MANIFEST as reused_from, with the source report's created_at.
- Copy 'steps' and any reused_from entries into the tracked <tag>_summary.json manifest block.

As defence in depth, have evaluation/report.collect() take a run-start time and skip or flag (stale: true) any section whose created_at is earlier.

The current e2/e4 tracked summaries should have their ablation_ann and locomo_retrieval_ann sections removed. Those sections are baseline data.

confirmed.title: Retrieval metrics come from a different ranking and candidate pool than the context and the product
confirmed.scenario: run_query scores Recall/MRR/nDCG/pool_hit/correct_top1 on rag.search(limit=min(pool,100)), but builds the answer context from rag.search(limit=top_k). In rag.search the fusion depth is min(pool, max(20, 4*limit)), and fused[:pool] is chosen by that depth, so the depth depends on limit. With pool 100 (the default reranked pool in e2/e4, or --candidate-limit 100), the metric search fuses at depth 100 while the context and shipped calls with limit=5 fuse at depth 20. Probe on the dev split (HashEmbedder plus OverlapReranker fakes): fusion-only vector_graph at candidate_limit 100 had a different top-5 in 19 of 83 queries (fusion only, so no reranker ties are involved), and hybrid_full handed the reranker a different candidate set in 8 of 83 queries. Recall@5, pool_hit and correct_top1 therefore describe a configuration the product never runs, and they disagree with correct_grounded/correct_first, which come from the context. locomo.py:143-144 has the same problem: hybrid modes run with limit=min(pool,100), so hybrid_reranked (pool 100) and hybrid_fusion with an explicit pool above 20 do not match the product.
confirmed.fix: Compute metrics and context from a single search at the product limit. One way: have search() expose the full ordered pool (for example in diagnostics) and have context() accept precomputed hits. Another: make the fusion depth independent of limit (pass the protocol's top_k as a separate fusion_limit) so limit=pool and limit=top_k give the same ordering. Add a regression test asserting that the top-k of the deep call equals the top-k of the shallow call.

verdict.evidence:
I traced the code and confirmed the finding with a probe. In main/retrieval/rag.py:340 the fusion depth is `depth = min(pool, max(20, 4 * limit))`. Lines 341-349 rank the head (channel rank <= depth) ahead of the deeper candidates, overwrite `scores` with the head-only sums, then cut to `fused[:pool]`. That means `limit` changes three things: the fusion order, which candidates go to the reranker, and the fusion scores the reranker uses to break ties. evaluation/ablation.py:63 takes Recall/MRR/nDCG/pool_hit/correct_top1 from `rag.search(limit=min(pool,100), candidate_limit=pool)`. Lines 66-67 build the context, and from it correct_grounded/correct_first, using `limit=protocol.top_k` (5). With pool=100 the metric call fuses at depth 100 while the context call, like a product call with limit=5, fuses at depth 20. With pool=20 both calls use depth 20, so the baseline is not affected. Pool 100 happens with `--candidate-limit 100` (the measure_all e2 tag) or with `--candidate-limit default`, where reranked arms get 100.

Probe: scratchpad/review/probe_depth.py, dev split, 90 queries, HashEmbedder + OverlapReranker, R@5 over answerable queries. It compares the top 5 of the deep metric call with the top 5 of a limit=5 call at the same pool.
- candidate_limit 20: every arm had 0/90 queries with a different top 5, and identical R@5.
- candidate_limit 100: vector 0/90 and vector_reranker 0/90 (identical). vector_graph 20/90 differ, R@5 0.167 deep vs 0.094 shallow. That is a 77% relative gain in the reported metric that the product never delivers, and it would show up as a fake improvement from baseline to e2. vector_graph_reranker 5/90 differ (R@5 equal). hybrid_full, the shipped path, 42/90 differ, R@5 0.729 vs 0.713.

Recall@5, MRR, pool_hit and correct_top1 therefore describe a different configuration than the context-based correct_grounded/correct_first in the same row. evaluation/locomo.py:143-144 has the same pattern: hybrid modes use `limit=min(mode_pool,100)`, so hybrid_reranked and any explicit pool above 20 measure depth-100 fusion instead of the product's depth 20. The finding's per-query counts (19 and 8 of 83) differ slightly from mine because of a different denominator, but the claim holds.
verdict.fix: Make the fusion depth independent of the `limit` used for metrics. Minimal change: add an optional `fusion_limit=None` keyword to `MemoryRAG.search` (rag.py:246). Compute `depth = min(pool, max(20, 4 * (limit if fusion_limit is None else fusion_limit)))`, so product behavior stays the same when it is None. Then pass `fusion_limit=protocol.top_k` in the metric search at evaluation/ablation.py:63 and in the hybrid search at locomo.py:143. The deep list then has the same order as the top_k call, and its tail still supports Recall@20 and pool_hit. Also add a regression test: for pool=100 and a fusion-only arm plus a reranked arm, assert that `search(limit=100, fusion_limit=5)[:5] == search(limit=5)[:5]`. Treat any e2 or `default`-pool reports produced so far as not comparable for the vector_graph and hybrid arms.

confirmed.title: A superseding statement that a channel found below the pool cut is never injected, while one no channel found is
confirmed.scenario: The injection filter checks `s not in scores`. `scores` holds every channel candidate, including the ones that `fused = fused[:pool]` (line 349) has already cut. When a superseding memory matched some channel weakly (for example a keyword-only hit ranked past the pool), it is in `scores` but not in `fused`. It is therefore neither injected nor present for `_structured_order`, so the stale statement stays at rank 1. A successor that shares no words with the query does get injected and promoted. I reproduced this with a scratch probe (scratchpad/review/probe_inject5.py: tests/test_structured_rerank fixtures, 6 distractors, candidate_limit=3, query 'Which city do we live in, renting a flat?'). With the successor 'Moved to Porto last March' the result is new-home first (supersedes:old-home). With the better match 'Moved to Porto last March, renting' the result is old-home first and new-home is gone. The same happens with the default pool of 100 on corpora with more than 100 fused candidates.
confirmed.fix: Test membership against the truncated pool: `fused_set = set(fused)` and `... for s in successors if s not in fused_set`. When appending, keep real fusion data for successors that are already in scores: `scores.setdefault(identifier, 0.0); details.setdefault(identifier, {})` instead of overwriting with 0.0 and {}. Add a regression test where the successor is a deep, single-channel hit.

verdict.evidence: The finding is real. In main/retrieval/rag.py, `scores` is filled from every channel candidate (lines ~325-330), and each channel can return up to `pool` ids, so the union can be bigger than `pool`. Line 349 (`fused = fused[:pool]`) truncates the list, but `scores` keeps the ids that were cut. The validity step runs by default (STRUCTURE_STEPS = {'graph','validity','chain'}, line 122). It calls `self._validity(user_id, fused, allowed)` to find stale statements in the truncated pool. The injection filter at line 365 is `for s in successors if s not in scores`, so a successor that a channel retrieved but the cut removed is skipped. It is not in `fused`, so it is not reranked and `_structured_order` cannot promote it. A successor that no channel found is not in `scores`, so it does get injected. I re-ran the existing probe (scratchpad/review/probe_inject5.py, which uses the tests/test_structured_rerank fixtures with candidate_limit=3) and got exactly what the finding describes. Case A ('Moved to Porto last March', matched by no channel): new-home is ranked first with `supersedes:old-home` and pool size 4. Case B ('Moved to Porto last March, renting', a keyword hit ranked past the cut): old-home is ranked first, new-home is missing entirely, and pool size is 3. So a stale fact is returned as current only because its successor matched the query better. With the default reranked pool of 100, this happens on corpora where the channels together return more than 100 ids. Severity stays medium: the step is on by default and it silently returns stale facts, but it needs a large candidate union or a small candidate_limit.
verdict.fix: In main/retrieval/rag.py at line 365, test membership against the truncated pool instead of `scores`: build `pool_ids = set(fused)` before the injection block and use `for s in successors if s not in pool_ids`. When appending, keep any real fusion data: `scores.setdefault(identifier, 0.0); details.setdefault(identifier, {})` instead of overwriting both with 0.0 and {}. Add a regression test based on probe_inject5 case B, where the successor is a single-channel keyword hit ranked past candidate_limit; old-home must not come first and new-home must be present with `supersedes:old-home`.

confirmed.title: Abstention stemmer keeps doubled consonants, so the numeric-slot anchor misses and answerable questions are refused
confirmed.scenario: _stem('running')='runn' but _stem('run')='run'. The same happens for swimming/swim, jogging/jog, shopping/shop, stopped/stop and planned/plan. For frequency, money, duration and distance slots, line 417 builds anchors from the question's content words and keeps only evidence sentences whose stemmed words share an anchor. Probed with ask --abstain semantics (abstain_threshold=0.0, reranker applied, logit 1.0): 'How often do I go running?' + 'I run three times a week.' gives unfilled_frequency_slot. 'How often do I go swimming?' + 'I swim twice a week.' gives unfilled_frequency_slot. 'How long did my run take?' + 'Running the loop took 45 minutes.' gives unfilled_duration_slot. 'How far is my jogging route?' + 'I jog 5 km every morning.' gives unfilled_distance_slot. The rule refuses answerable questions even though a filler is present, which also lowers measured correct-answer rates for the abstention arm.
confirmed.fix: In _stem, after stripping 'ing'/'ed', collapse a final doubled consonant (e.g. if len(word)>=3 and word[-1]==word[-2] and word[-1] not in 'lsz': word=word[:-1]). Alternatively, compare anchors on a 4-character prefix as well as the stem. Add regression cases for run/running, swim/swimming and shop/shopping.

verdict.evidence:
I confirmed this by reading the code and running a probe. In main/retrieval/generation.py:224-237, `_stem` removes 'ing'/'ed' but leaves a doubled final consonant in place. Results: running->runn, swimming->swimm, jogging->jogg, shopping->shopp, stopped->stopp, planned->plann, while the base forms stay run, swim, jog, shop, stop, plan.

For frequency, money, duration and distance slots, `_slot_evidence` (lines 414-426) only keeps evidence sentences whose window shares a stemmed anchor with the question's content words. A mismatch therefore throws out sentences that do contain the answer, and `abstention_reason` returns unfilled_<slot>_slot.

Probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-josephremingstonl-Downloads-code-capstone/2d91e859-4acd-4fbf-99c1-146f2e2aa197/scratchpad/review/stem_probe.py. It calls `abstention_reason` with threshold 0.0, reranker status applied and a logit of 1.0:
- 'How often do I go running?' + 'I run three times a week.' -> unfilled_frequency_slot
- 'How often do I go swimming?' + 'I swim twice a week.' -> unfilled_frequency_slot
- 'How long did my run take?' + 'Running the loop took 45 minutes.' -> unfilled_duration_slot
- 'How far is my jogging route?' + 'I jog 5 km every morning.' -> unfilled_distance_slot
- 'How much did I spend shopping?' + 'I spent $200 at the shop.' -> unfilled_money_slot

Controls pass: 'How often do I run?' + 'I run...' answers, and so does 'go running' + 'go running'.

Impact: the rule is opt-in (`ask --abstain`, `abstain_threshold`). It is wired into the evaluation harness at evaluation/systems.py:68, so the abstention arm refuses some answerable questions. evaluation/metrics.py scores those rows 0, which pushes correct-answer rates down and refusal counts up for the arm. That fits medium, not high: it fails closed and produces no wrong answer.
verdict.fix:
At the end of `_stem`, after the suffix and trailing-'e' handling, collapse a doubled final consonant every time, not only when a suffix was stripped. Question words and evidence words then stay consistent, for example add/added both become 'ad'. Change it to: `word = word[:-1] if word.endswith('e') and len(word) > 3 else word; if len(word) >= 3 and word[-1] == word[-2] and word[-1] not in 'aeiouylsz': word = word[:-1]; return word`.

I tested this by monkeypatching `_stem` in scratch/review/stem_fix.py. All four failing cases then answer, and tests/test_abstention.py still passes 20/20 against the unpatched code (the patch only lived in the scratch script). Add regression cases for run/running, swim/swimming, jog/jogging and shop/shopping.

confirmed.title: 'How much time ... spend' is classified as a money slot, so time answers are rejected
confirmed.scenario: _SLOT_QUESTIONS is checked in order and 'money' comes before 'duration'. The money pattern '^how\s+much\b.*\b(?:...spend|spent...)' matches before the duration alternative '^how\s+much\s+time\b' is tried. 'How much time did I spend on the project?' + 'I spent three weeks on the project.' gives unfilled_money_slot. 'How much time do I spend on homework?' + 'I spend 2 hours on homework every night.' also gives unfilled_money_slot, because _BARE_AMOUNT deliberately excludes numbers followed by a time unit. The extractive answer abstains on a fully answered question.
confirmed.fix: Exclude time from the money pattern (e.g. '^how\s+much\s+(?!time\b)...'), or move the 'duration' entry ahead of 'money' in _SLOT_QUESTIONS. Add a test for 'How much time did I spend ...'.

verdict.evidence:
Confirmed with a probe (scratchpad/review/slot_time.py) that calls the real question_slot() and abstention_reason() with a context where the reranker was applied and scored 3.0:
- 'How much time did I spend on the project?' + 'I spent three weeks on the project.' gives slot=money and unfilled_money_slot.
- 'How much time do I spend on homework?' + 'I spend 2 hours on homework every night.' gives slot=money and unfilled_money_slot.
- 'How much time do I spend commuting?' + 'My commute takes 45 minutes each way.' gives slot=money and unfilled_money_slot.
- Control: 'How much time does it take to bake the bread?' gives slot=duration and answers. Without spend/pay/cost words the duration pattern is reached.

Why it happens: question_slot() (generation.py:245) returns the first matching entry in _SLOT_QUESTIONS. The money regex at line 211 ('^how\s+much\b.*\b(?:...spend|spent|spends...)') sits before the duration entry at line 215, which has the '^how\s+much\s+time\b' alternative. In _filled_by, money is filled only by _MONEY (currency symbols and words) or an anchored _BARE_AMOUNT. _BARE_AMOUNT rejects numbers followed by a time unit (line 145), so duration evidence can never fill the slot. The default ABSTAIN_THRESHOLD=0.0 still runs the slot check, so the extractive answer abstains on a question it fully answers. The rule is opt-in (ask --abstain / slot rule v2), which caps the impact. But 'how much time did I spend on X' is a common personal-memory phrasing, for example in LongMemEval-style questions, so it also skews abstention and accuracy numbers when the rule is evaluated. No test covers 'how much time'.
verdict.fix: In main/retrieval/generation.py _SLOT_QUESTIONS, move the ('duration', ...) entry ahead of ('money', ...). Alternatively, add a negative lookahead to the money regex: r"^how\s+much\s+(?!time\b).*\b(?:cost|...)". The duration branch already returns None for aggregation and date-arithmetic questions. Add a test asserting question_slot('How much time did I spend on the project?') == 'duration', and that abstention_reason does not abstain when the evidence is 'I spent three weeks on the project.'

confirmed.title: Money slot fires on 'what/which ... bill/fee/budget/cost/rent' questions whose answer is not an amount
confirmed.scenario: The second money alternative '^(?:what|which)(?:'s|\s+is|...)?\s+(?:[\w'-]+\s+){0,3}?(?:price|salary|rent|fee|fees|bill|budget|wage|cost)(?![\w-])' treats any what/which question that mentions one of these nouns as asking for an amount. Probed results: 'Which bill did I forget to pay?' + 'I forgot to pay the electricity bill again.' gives unfilled_money_slot. 'What budget app do I use?' + 'I track spending with YNAB, the budget app.' gives unfilled_money_slot. 'Which fee did the bank waive?' + 'The bank waived the overdraft fee.' gives unfilled_money_slot. 'What cost me the most last month?' + 'The car repair was the biggest expense last month.' gives unfilled_money_slot. 'What is the rent like in my area?' gives unfilled_money_slot. All of these are answerable questions refused by a rule documented as only targeting stated amounts.
confirmed.fix: Restrict the alternative to amount-seeking forms. Require the noun to be the question's head followed by end of question, 'of'/'for' or a possessor, as in 'what is my rent', 'what was the price of X' or 'what's Ana's salary'. Reject 'which <noun>', '<noun> + another noun' (budget app) and 'what cost' as a verb. Add negative tests for these questions.

verdict.evidence:
The finding is real: I reproduced it. The problem is the second money alternative in _SLOT_QUESTIONS at main/retrieval/generation.py:213-214. Its pattern is `^(?:what|which)(?:'s|\s+is|\s+was|\s+are|\s+were)?\s+(?:[\w'-]+\s+){0,3}?(?:price|salary|rent|fee|fees|bill|budget|wage|cost)(?![\w-])`. It returns slot 'money' for any what/which question that contains one of those nouns within the first four words. Nothing checks that the noun is the head of an amount-seeking question. The only extra filter question_slot() applies to money is `_AGGREGATION` (line 255). The entity slot, by contrast, has an `_ENTITY_HEAD` check for nouns used as modifiers (line 250). _filled_by then needs a currency token, or an anchored bare number (line 448), so evidence without a number abstains.

Probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-josephremingstonl-Downloads-code-capstone/2d91e859-4acd-4fbf-99c1-146f2e2aa197/scratchpad/review/money_probe.py. It uses the tests/test_abstention.py `decide` helper with the reranker applied and logit 3.0. Each of these questions got slot=money and returned unfilled_money_slot:
- 'Which bill did I forget to pay?' with 'I forgot to pay the electricity bill again.'
- 'What budget app do I use?' with 'I track spending with YNAB, the budget app.'
- 'Which fee did the bank waive?'
- 'What cost me the most last month?'
- 'What is the rent like in my area?'
- 'What price range am I looking at...'
- 'What salary negotiation tips did my mentor give?'
- 'What streaming bill did I cancel?'

The control 'What is my rent?' with 'Rent went up to 1,450 a month.' correctly answers (None).

I am lowering severity from medium to low. The rule only runs when you opt in: `answer(abstain_threshold=None)` is the default. In the CLI it needs `ask --abstain --generator extractive`, a flag labelled experimental. In the evaluation it needs `--abstain-threshold`. The default answer path and the Gemini path are unaffected. The failure is a false refusal ('Insufficient memory evidence.'), with no crash or data loss. Abstention metrics show the rule's actual behaviour, so they are not misleading.
verdict.fix:
In question_slot (main/retrieval/generation.py ~line 249), add a head guard for the second money alternative, like the `_ENTITY_HEAD` check for entities. Keep the 'how much ...' alternative as it is. For the what/which alternative:
- Reject 'which <noun>'.
- Require the money noun to end the question, or to be followed by 'of'/'for'/'per'/'like a' (or by a verb or possessive pronoun after a possessor), as in 'what is my rent', "what's Ana's salary" or 'what was the price of X'.
- Reject it when another content noun comes straight after it (budget app, salary negotiation, price range).
- Drop bare 'cost' from the noun list, or require a determiner/possessor before it, so the verb in 'what cost me ...' does not match.

Example: change the alternative to `^(?:what)(?:'s|\s+is|\s+was|\s+are|\s+were)\s+(?:(?:my|his|her|their|your|our|the)\s+|[\w-]+(?:'s|s')\s+){1,2}(?:[\w-]+\s+)?(?:price|salary|rent|fee|fees|bill|budget|wage|cost)(?:\s*\??\s*$|\s+(?:of|for|per|at|on|now|these days)\b)`.

Add negative tests to tests/test_abstention.py for the questions in the probe, with question_slot(q) expected to be None.

confirmed.title: Questions asking the store to recall a user fact are now kept as EPISODIC for 90 days and rank above the fact itself
confirmed.scenario: Every uncertain or interrogative user turn that contains 'my' or 'I' (once the inversion is stripped) now goes through _discloses() and comes back EPISODIC. Memory lookups are interrogatives with 'my', so they are caught too. I ran this probe (scratchpad review/probe_q.py): ingest 'My dog is named Biscuit.' (SEMANTIC), then 'What was my dog's name again?' and 'Wait, what is my dog called?'. Both questions become EPISODIC/short_term with expires_at = +90 days. Before this change they were TEMPORARY/working and expired after 1 hour. Twenty days later, store.search("what is my dog's name") returns the two questions at ranks 1 and 2 and the actual fact at rank 3. Every recall attempt a user makes adds another non-answer memory that pushes the answer down in retrieval and generation context for 3 months.
confirmed.fix: Do not treat information-seeking wh-questions as disclosures when their only first-person content is the thing being asked for. For example, return TEMPORARY when the text matches ^(?:what|where|when|who|which|how)\b[^.!]*\b(?:is|was|are|were|did|do)\s+(?:my|i)\b or contains a recall cue (again|remind me|did i (?:tell|say|mention)). Only call it a disclosure if a first-person clause remains after that question clause is removed. Add regression tests for recall questions next to the 'Do you know if I need a visa' cases.

verdict.evidence: Reproduced and compared against HEAD. In main/domain/classification.py:108-112, any uncertain/interrogative user turn now returns EPISODIC when _discloses() is true. self_disclosure() in main/domain/text_rules.py removes only inverted auxiliaries followed by i/we ('did I', 'can I'). It does not remove 'my <noun>' in wh-questions, so 'What was my dog's name again?' still matches \b(?:my|our)\s+\w. lifecycle.py:55-58 then gives user EPISODIC short-term records archive_age_days (90). The existing probe review/probe_q.py on the working tree prints both recall questions as episodic/short_term with expires_at=2027-01-10. store.search("what is my dog's name", now=+20d) returns the two questions at ranks 1 and 2 and 'My dog is named Biscuit.' at rank 3. I extracted HEAD's main/ into scratch (review/head) and ran the same probe with python -I: both questions come out temporary/working, expire after about 1 hour, and the search returns only the fact. So the regression is real and caused by this change. Severity is lower than claimed. The design deliberately keeps 'my X' questions (tests/test_user_disclosure_retention.py expects 'What are some ways to keep my living room dust-free?' to be EPISODIC/90d), so the gap is specifically recall questions that add no new information. RAGPipeline.search defaults to limit=5 and can apply a reranker, so the fact only falls out of context after several recall questions pile up, or at small limits. The outcome is retrieval noise and context displacement, not a crash or data loss.
verdict.fix: In MemoryClassifier (classification.py, before the uncertain() branch at line 108, or inside _discloses), return TEMPORARY for recall-style questions whose only first-person content is the thing being asked about. For example, when lowered matches r"^(?:\w+,?\s+)?(?:what|where|when|who|which|how)\b[^.!?]*\b(?:is|was|are|were|'s)\s+(?:my|our)\b" or a recall cue such as r"\b(?:again|remind me|did i (?:tell|say|mention)|do you remember)\b", strip that question clause and call self_disclosure only on what remains. confirmed.title: 90-day retention keys on category EPISODIC, so temporal-keyword requests and the legacy/ML path are kept about 6x longer

The classifier also gives EPISODIC through its broad keyword fallback: episodic_patterns match today/tomorrow/last/next, 'on|at <digit>' and month names (including the modal 'may' and the verb 'march', case-insensitive). In expiry_for, use 90 days only when that flag is set. Otherwise check self_disclosure(record.content) and skip it when the classifier is legacy. Keep the 14-day window for generic temporal-keyword EPISODIC records.

verdict.evidence: Confirmed with a probe (scratchpad/review/probe_life.py, MemoryCore().process with role='user' at a fixed timestamp). main/domain/lifecycle.py:57 sets `user_event = record.role == 'user' and record.category is MemoryCategory.EPISODIC` and gives such records archive_age_days (90) in place of 14. confirmed.title: Protocol records a single reranked pool even though fusion-only arms ran with a different pool
confirmed.scenario: protocol_record gets resolved_pool=resolve_pool(top_k, candidate_limit), which defaults to rerank=True. With --candidate-limit default (e2/e4), the vector and vector_graph arms actually used pool 20 (row pool_size is 20 for all 270 rows in e4), while results.md, SUMMARY.md and summary.json _protocol.resolved_pool say 'Candidate pool: 100' for every arm. The Pool hit and Reranker recovery columns therefore set hit@20 beside hit@100 under one label. locomo.py:118 records the same single reranked pool while hybrid_fusion ran at 20.
confirmed.fix: Record resolved_pool per arm or mode, e.g. {arm: resolve_pool(top_k, candidate_limit, rerank=ARMS[arm]['rerank'])}. Print the per-arm pool in the markdown tables and in report.collect's _protocol.

verdict.evidence:
Traced the code and checked it against the committed e4 outputs, which ran with candidate_limit=None (the 'default' setting).

Code path:
- evaluation/ablation.py:61 resolves the pool per arm with `resolve_pool(top_k, candidate_limit, rerank=options['rerank'])`.
- evaluation/systems.py:39-43 sends None to rag.default_pool. That gives 100 when rerank is on and min(200, max(20, 4*limit)) = 20 when it is off (top_k=5).
- ablation.py:203 records `resolved_pool=resolve_pool(protocol.top_k, protocol.candidate_limit)` with no rerank argument, so it always stores the reranked value.
- markdown() at ablation.py:150 and report.py:131/167 print that one value for every arm.
- locomo.py:118 does the same thing (`pool = resolve_pool(...)`, recorded at line 151), while line 141 runs each mode with its own mode_pool.

Data from docs/reports/e4:
- ablation/results.json has protocol candidate_limit=None and resolved_pool=100. Counting rows by (arm, pool_size) gives vector→20 for all 270, vector_graph→20 for all 270, and the reranked arms →100 (266 rows), with a few at 73/94.
- ablation_dev shows the same pattern (vector arms 20 ×90).
- ablation/results.md line 3 says "Candidate pool: 100", and SUMMARY.md says "Controlled benchmark, test split (pool 100 ...)". Both tables put vector Pool hit 99.2% (hit@20) next to vector_reranker 100% (hit@100).
- locomo_retrieval.json has protocol resolved_pool=100, but hybrid_fusion pool_hit is 0.696 (the pool-20 number quoted in default_pool's docstring) and hybrid_reranked is 0.919 (pool 100).

The per-row metrics are computed correctly. The problem is the protocol label: it misstates the pool used by the fusion-only arms and modes, so the Pool hit and Reranker recovery comparisons across arms look like they share a pool when they don't. The label is only wrong when candidate_limit is None. With an explicit integer (the default '20', or e2's 100) every arm uses the same pool and the record is correct, so the impact is limited to misleading metrics. It does not cause a crash or wrong per-arm numbers.
verdict.fix: Record the pool per arm or mode instead of one value. In ablation.py:203: `resolved_pool={arm: resolve_pool(protocol.top_k, protocol.candidate_limit, rerank=ARMS[arm]['rerank']) for arm in arms}`. In locomo.py:118/151: `{mode: resolve_pool(protocol.top_k, protocol.candidate_limit, rerank=mode == 'hybrid_reranked') for mode in modes if mode.startswith('hybrid')}`. Then update markdown() (ablation.py:150) and report.py:131/167 to print the pool for each arm, for example as a Pool column or as text like 'pool: reranked 100 / fusion-only 20'. Alternatively, keep the scalar only when all values are equal.

confirmed.title: report_delta compares snapshots without checking that dataset or protocol match
confirmed.scenario: load() returns only 'flat' and ignores the manifest. The working-tree gold_queries.json now hashes to a93ca70f..., while baseline, e2 and e4 all record dataset_sha256 1cba69ec... (the dataset was rebuilt with diversified unanswerable seeds). The next tag (e.g. e6) compared against baseline will print deltas across two different benchmarks with no warning. The same happens when pool, ann, structure or abstain settings differ.
confirmed.fix: Read payload['manifest'] and each section's _protocol. Refuse, or print a loud warning, when dataset_sha256 differs, and list protocol fields that differ before the delta table. Also report keys present in only one snapshot instead of silently dropping them.

verdict.evidence:
The finding holds for the dataset hash. It only partly holds for protocol settings.

1. `load()` in `/Users/josephremingstonl/Downloads/code/capstone/scripts/report_delta.py` (line 18) returns only `json.loads(...)['flat']`. `main()` (lines 27-34) never looks at `payload['manifest']`.
2. `scripts/measure_all.py` (lines 84 and 91) writes `manifest.dataset_sha256` into every summary, so the information is there to check.
3. baseline, e2 and e4 all record dataset_sha256 `1cba69ec...`. Running `shasum` on the working-tree `evaluation/datasets/gold_queries.json` gives `a93ca70ff6d4...`. The next snapshot taken from this tree will record a different hash.
4. I ran `report_delta.py baseline e4 --match ablation.`. It printed the delta table with no warning, and the dataset hash never appears because it is a string inside the manifest.
5. Protocol settings are partly visible. `_protocol.resolved_pool` (20 vs 100) and the `ann` bool are flattened as numbers, so they show up as delta rows. A row like `ablation._protocol.resolved_pool +80` is easy to miss among about 600 metric rows. `abstain_threshold`, which is None in these snapshots, and any non-numeric setting are dropped.
6. The two snapshots have different key sets. e4 has 10 keys that baseline lacks (for example `ablation.*.correct_first_answerable`). The `set(before) & set(after)` intersection drops them without saying so.

Result: deltas between snapshots built on different gold sets print as if they were comparable. That gives misleading metrics, though no data loss or crash. I am keeping severity at medium because the script exists to produce these comparisons and the dataset was in fact rebuilt. The protocol part is lower risk because the numeric settings already appear as rows.
verdict.fix:
In `report_delta.py`, change `load()` to return the whole payload. In `main()`:

- Compare `before['manifest'].get('dataset_sha256')` with the same field in `after`. If they differ, stop with `SystemExit('dataset_sha256 differs: ...')`, unless the user passes an explicit `--allow-dataset-mismatch` flag, in which case print a loud warning first.
- Before the delta table, print every `_protocol` key whose value differs between the two snapshots, from the sections or from flat keys containing `._protocol.`. Also leave those `_protocol` keys out of the metric rows.
- After the table, list the keys that appear in only one snapshot, so dropped keys are reported instead of disappearing.

confirmed.title: MANIFEST cannot identify the code or command that produced a snapshot
confirmed.scenario: The manifest stores only `git rev-parse --short HEAD` and a dirty flag. baseline, e2 and e4 all record git_head '12dbc04' with dirty_tree true, even though rag.py and indexes.py changed substantially between them (F1/F2/F4/F5). The step commands and arguments (--candidate-limit, --structure, --ann, --abstain-threshold) are not recorded either: outcomes hold only name, exit code and seconds. A tagged snapshot cannot be tied to the code that produced it or re-run.
confirmed.fix: Record a hash of `git diff HEAD` plus the untracked file list, or save the patch into the snapshot. Record sys.argv and the full command for each step in MANIFEST.

verdict.evidence:
Half of the finding holds and half does not.

What holds: the snapshot cannot be tied to the code that produced it. In /Users/josephremingstonl/Downloads/code/capstone/scripts/measure_all.py, lines 80-85, MANIFEST gets only `git rev-parse --short HEAD` and `dirty = bool(git status --porcelain)`. It stores no hash of the diff and no list of untracked files. The real manifests confirm this. docs/reports/baseline, e2 and e4 MANIFEST.json all have git_head '12dbc04' and dirty_tree true, and every report's protocol.git_head is '12dbc04+dirty'. Yet the code differs between runs: baseline's protocol says default_pool_formula 'max(20, 4*limit)' and ann_exact_threshold 256, while e2/e4 say 'reranked: min(200, max(100, 4*limit))...' and 5000. Because scripts/ and most of the changed evaluation/ code are untracked or modified, no snapshot can be rebuilt from its manifest.

What does not hold: the claim that run settings are lost. The per-step `steps` entries are indeed only {step, exit_code, seconds}, and sys.argv is not saved. But every retrieval report inside the snapshot keeps its settings in `protocol`: candidate_limit, top_k, ann, abstain_threshold, structure ('none' in e2, 'default' in e4), resolved_pool, the models and reranker_threads. With those, plus the fixed plan in steps(), each command can be rebuilt.

No metric is computed wrongly here. The impact is reproducibility and audit only, so I rate it low, not medium.

Separate, more serious issue (outside this finding): snapshot() copies everything currently in docs/reports/, so files left over from earlier runs end up in later snapshots. e2 and e4 were run without --ann-arms, yet both contain ablation_ann/results.json (created_at 2026-10-12T01:15:01, from the baseline run) and locomo_retrieval_ann.json (candidate_limit 20, old pool formula). Anyone reading e2/e4 sees ANN numbers that came from the baseline run.
verdict.fix:
In snapshot(), at about line 83 of scripts/measure_all.py, also record:
- 'diff_sha256': sha256 of `git diff HEAD --binary` output
- 'untracked': `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, ideally with each file's sha256
- 'argv': sys.argv

Optionally, write the diff into the snapshot as code.patch.

In main(), add 'command': command to each outcome dict at line 124.

For the stale-file issue, either clear docs/reports/ output directories before the steps run, or copy only the outputs each planned step actually wrote (or skip any file older than the run's start time).

confirmed.title: Re-using a tag silently deletes the existing snapshot and overwrites its tracked summary
confirmed.scenario: snapshot() runs shutil.rmtree(target) whenever docs/reports/<tag> exists, and then overwrites evaluation/reports/<tag>_summary.json. Re-running `--tag baseline` by mistake, for example after code changes, permanently replaces the reference baseline that all deltas are measured against. docs/ is git-ignored, so the old snapshot cannot be recovered.
confirmed.fix: Refuse when the tag already exists unless --overwrite is passed. Alternatively, move the old snapshot to <tag>.prev-<timestamp>.

verdict.evidence: The code does what the finding says. In /Users/josephremingstonl/Downloads/code/capstone/scripts/measure_all.py, snapshot() at lines 71-73 runs `if target.exists(): shutil.rmtree(target)` on docs/reports/<tag> with no check and no backup. Lines 87-92 then write evaluation/reports/<tag>_summary.json with an unconditional write_text. main() offers no --overwrite or existence check, and the snapshot is taken only after every step has finished, so by then the live outputs under docs/reports/* are already replaced too. Neither copy can be recovered. `git check-ignore` confirms docs/ is ignored (.gitignore:13 `/docs/*`), and `git ls-files evaluation/reports | grep summary` returns nothing, so baseline_summary.json, e2_summary.json and e4_summary.json are untracked as well. The baseline/, e2/ and e4/ snapshots all exist on disk now. The risk is realistic: evaluation/README.md:11 gives `scripts/measure_all.py --tag baseline ...` as the command to copy, and PROGRESS.md and the user's memory say deltas must be compared only against tagged snapshots, which report_delta.py reads from evaluation/reports/<tag>_summary.json. Running that command again after a code change silently replaces the reference baseline, and every later delta is then measured against the new code. I lowered the severity to low because it needs an operator mistake and computes nothing wrong by itself. The new manifest's git_head and created_at would also show the replacement if someone checked.
verdict.fix: Add `parser.add_argument('--overwrite', action='store_true')` to main(). Before running any step, and only when not a dry run, check `if (REPORTS / args.tag).exists() or (ROOT/'evaluation'/'reports'/f'{args.tag}_summary.json').exists()`. If either exists and --overwrite is not set, call `parser.error(f'tag {args.tag!r} already exists; pass --overwrite')`. Doing the check before the run avoids an hours-long run that then fails at snapshot time. Another option is to rename the old directory and summary to <tag>.prev-<timestamp> instead of deleting them.

confirmed.title: The approximate-search arm never records whether LSH was actually used
confirmed.scenario: ApproximateVectorIndex falls back to an exact scan when allowed_ids <= max(limit, 400) or when radius-2 probing finds too few candidates, and it records the path in hits[0]['vector_index']. Neither run_query nor locomo.py stores that field. The benchmark has 456 memories and the vector limit is pool*3, so with any candidate_limit of 152 or more every query is exact. Historical queries (graph-only candidates) are always exact. LoCoMo conv-30 (369 text turns) is always exact. Probe with the fake embedder on the test split at pool 20 and 100: 245 exact_fallback, 23 allowed_below_target, 2 lsh. The 'approximate search' tables can therefore report exact-search numbers under an ANN label.
confirmed.fix: Add vector_algorithm=hits[0]['vector_index'].get('algorithm') and fallback to every row. Summarize the share of LSH, exact and exact_fallback per arm, and show it beside the ANN results. Optionally fail the ANN arm if LSH answered fewer than X% of queries.

verdict.evidence:
I followed the code end to end and confirmed the finding.

1. When protocol.ann is set, `build_rag` (evaluation/systems.py:47-49) passes `ann_exact_threshold=1`, with the comment "force LSH even on small benchmark corpora". `MemoryRAG.vector_index` therefore returns an `ApproximateVectorIndex`.
2. That index is built with the default `min_candidates=400` (main/storage/indexes.py:195). `search()` sets `target = max(limit, 400)`. It takes the exact path when `len(allowed_ids) <= target` (reason `allowed_below_target`). It only counts a search as LSH once the probes have gathered at least `target` allowed chunks. If radius 2 runs out first, it falls back to an exact scan (`exact_fallback`).
3. rag.py:293-296 calls `vectors.search(..., limit=pool * 3)` and copies `last_search` into every hit as `hit['vector_index']` (rag.py:442).
4. `run_query` (evaluation/ablation.py:56-82) never reads `hits[0]['vector_index']`. Neither does locomo.py (lines 143-150 store only the reranker status). report.py labels these tables only from `protocol['ann']`, as "approximate search" / exact=False.

Probe: scratchpad/review/ann_path_probe.py. It uses the HashEmbedder fake on the test split, the vector arm, every third query (90 queries), and `build_rag(..., Protocol(ann=True))`:
- pool 20: exact_fallback 84, allowed_below_target 5, lsh 1 (that one LSH search had 413 candidates)
- pool 100: the same counts
- pool 160: allowed_below_target 90/90. Here `limit = 480 > 456`, so every query is exact.

The benchmark has 456 memories and 456 chunks (checked with chunks.py). An LSH search can only complete after it has gathered at least 400 of the 456 chunks, which is 88% or more of the corpus. So even with a real embedder, which may reach LSH more often than the hash fake, the "approximate" arm is close to an exhaustive scan by construction. It cannot show LSH recall loss, and it never reports which path answered.

Result: the ablation_ann and locomo_retrieval_ann tables give near-exact or exact numbers under an ANN label. Anyone reading them would conclude that LSH costs no recall. That is a misleading metric. Retrieval in the product itself is unaffected, so this is medium severity, not high.
verdict.fix:
Minimal fix, in two parts:

1. **Record the path.** In evaluation/ablation.py `run_query` (and the matching row in evaluation/locomo.py), add:
```python
vi = top['vector_index'] if top else {}
'vector_algorithm': vi.get('algorithm')
'vector_fallback': vi.get('fallback')
```
Then add the share of lsh / exact / exact_fallback per arm to `summarize()`, and print it beside the ANN tables in `markdown()` and report.py.

2. **Make the arm actually exercise LSH.** Add `ann_min_candidates` to `Protocol` (for example `max(limit, 50)`) and pass it through `MemoryRAG` to the `ApproximateVectorIndex(min_candidates=...)` constructor.

Optionally, make the ANN arm fail or warn when LSH answered fewer than about 50% of semantic searches.

confirmed.title: LoCoMo is reported as untuned although it was used to choose the pool size; no held-out headline
confirmed.scenario: The docstring and report claim 'LoCoMo is never used to tune anything'. But default_pool's docstring states the pool of 100 was chosen from a LoCoMo audit, and PROGRESS.md says F2 was designed on conversations 1-3, with only conversations 4-5 held out. locomo.run reports metrics over all 10 conversations with no split, so the headline hybrid_reranked Recall@5 that feeds SUMMARY and the deltas includes tuning data. retention.py makes the same 'no fitting' claim although F3 (90-day self-disclosure rule) was developed against LongMemEval failures.
confirmed.fix: Add a tuning/held-out partition to locomo.run (for example conversations 1-3 as tuning) and use held-out metrics as the headline in report.collect. Correct the docstring and protocol text in locomo.py and retention.py to state what was used for design.

verdict.evidence:
The finding holds. The size of the bias is small, so I'm downgrading it from medium to low.

1. evaluation/locomo.py:9 says "LoCoMo is never used to tune anything." That is contradicted in two places:
   - main/retrieval/rag.py:29: the default_pool docstring justifies DEFAULT_POOL_FLOOR = 100 with a "LoCoMo audit: a pool of 20 holds gold evidence 69.6% of the time, 100 holds 91.9%".
   - PROGRESS.md:38 says F2 (pool 20 -> 100) was designed on LoCoMo conversations 1-3, and that only conversations 4-5 "were never used for tuning".
2. locomo.run (locomo.py:112-160) scores every loaded conversation (`json.loads(payload)[:limit_conversations]`, which is all 10 by default) with no tuning/held-out split. report.collect (report.py:134-140) takes `report['metrics']` for each mode as is, and render_summary publishes that number as the LoCoMo headline. So the headline hybrid_reranked Recall@5 includes the three conversations used to make the design choice, while the docstring presents the result as fully external.
3. evaluation/retention.py:118 has the same problem: the protocol string says "All oracle examples ... no fitting", but PROGRESS.md:28 shows F3 (90-day self-disclosure rule) was developed against LongMemEval, with a separate held-out figure (90.6% overall vs 90.4% held-out). The report covers all examples and gives no split.

Why low and not medium: the design agents' own held-out numbers show almost no inflation. On LoCoMo, Recall@5 went .561 -> .669 on tuning conversations 1-3 and .554 -> .658 on held-out conversations 4-5. On LongMemEval, retention was 90.6% overall vs 90.4% held-out. Only one hyperparameter (the pool size) was chosen from 3 of 10 conversations. The real defect is the false "never tuned / no fitting" claim, which misrepresents what the numbers mean, rather than a materially inflated metric. Nothing crashes and no data is affected.
verdict.fix:
Minimal fix: correct the claims.
- In locomo.py, change the docstring to say: "Conversations 1-3 (conv-26, conv-30, conv-41 by file order) were used to choose the reranker pool (F2); the other conversations are held out."
- In retention.py, change the protocol text to: "the F3 self-disclosure rule was designed against LongMemEval failures; no model is fitted at evaluation time".

Better fix:
- In locomo.run, tag each row with `split = 'tuning' if conversation_index < 3 else 'held_out'` and add `metrics_by_split` next to `metrics`.
- In report.collect/render_summary, show held-out Recall@5 as the LoCoMo headline, with the all-conversation figure labelled as including tuning data.
- Do the same in retention.py for whatever partition F3 used as held out.

unverified.title: fusion_score/score mix shallow (head) and deep RRF scales; reranker ties broken on inconsistent scores
unverified.scenario: `scores.update(head)` replaces scores only for candidates that have some rank <= depth. Every appended candidate keeps its full deep-RRF score plus the agreement bonus. A non-head candidate found by all three channels at ranks around 21 to 25 scores about 0.0123+0.004, while a head candidate found only by graph at rank 20 scores about 0.0025. Hits returned after reranking therefore report fusion_score values that do not follow the fused order. evaluation/ablation.py's top_fusion_score and context()['scores'][id]['fusion'] compare numbers that are not on the same scale. The reranker tie-break `-scores[key]` (line 415) can also put a deep candidate ahead of a head candidate. `signals` still lists deep ranks whose contributions are not counted in `score`.
unverified.fix: Keep one consistent score. Either store the head score in a separate field (`head_score`) and use the fused position (`fused.index`) as the reranker tie-break, or give non-head candidates a score strictly below every head score (for example rank them by deep score but report `score` as the shallow sum, which is 0 for them).

unverified.title: Reranker-fallback order can differ from rerank=False when memories have several chunks, contrary to the 'wider pool never reorders' guarantee
unverified.scenario: The semantic channel asks for `limit=pool*3` chunks and then dedupes by memory. With rerank=False the pool is 20, so 60 chunks are fetched. With the reranker on and failing, the pool is 100, so 300 chunks are fetched. If memories are long (more than one 1000-char chunk each), 60 chunks can cover fewer than 20 distinct memories, while 300 chunks fill ranks 1-20. In the fallback case the head (rank <= depth=20) therefore gains extra semantic votes, and the top-k can differ from the rerank=False result. Under ANN the vector `target` (`max(limit, min_candidates)`) also changes with pool, which changes early stopping. The existing test uses one-chunk memories only, so it misses this.
unverified.fix: Fetch the semantic channel at a depth independent of the pool for the head, for example request `max(pool, depth)*3` and build the depth-limited head from a run requested with `depth*3`. Or derive the head's semantic ranks from the first `depth` distinct memories of a single deeper request and document that. Add a test with multi-chunk memories.

unverified.title: Historical (as_of/known_at) semantic search re-syncs the vector index to the snapshot subset, evicting the user's other vectors (pre-existing, now also forces LSH rebuild)
unverified.scenario: With as_of or known_at set, `corpus = records`, which holds only the graph-sourced snapshots with summary=None. `vectors.sync(corpus)` then runs VectorIndex.sync, which deletes every chunk not in that subset (indexes.py line 130) and re-embeds snapshot texts whose digest changed because the summary was dropped. The next present-time query must re-embed the user's whole corpus. For an ANN-sized user (5000 or more memories), the historical call picks the exact index because len(corpus) is small, so the next present query also changes the LSH fingerprint and triggers a full bucket rebuild. Results stay correct, but every alternation between historical and present queries costs a full re-embed.
unverified.fix: For historical queries, sync the full current corpus (as in the present-time path), or skip sync and search only vectors that already exist. Embed snapshot texts under separate chunk ids, or search them with an ad-hoc in-memory exact scan, instead of overwriting the persistent index.

unverified.title: Common unit spellings missing from duration/distance fillers ('11h', '12 kms', '90 mins' ok but 'h' not)
unverified.scenario: _TIME_UNIT has no bare 'h', and _LENGTH_UNIT matches 'km' but not 'kms'; the trailing \b fails on 'kms'. 'How long was my flight?' + 'My flight was 11h.' gives unfilled_duration_slot. 'How far is my commute?' + 'My commute is 12 kms.' gives unfilled_distance_slot. In both cases --abstain refuses an answered question.
unverified.fix: Add 'h|hrs?' (digit-adjacent only, to avoid matching words) to the duration unit list. Make the km alternative 'kms?' in _LENGTH_UNIT.

unverified.title: search --candidate-limit help claims COGNIMEM_CANDIDATE_POOL / 100-floor default even when no reranking happens
unverified.scenario: `python -m main search q --mode semantic` (or graph, or --no-rerank) never reranks, because rag.search sets should_rerank = mode=='hybrid'. default_pool(rerank=False) then returns min(200, max(20, 4*limit)) and ignores COGNIMEM_CANDIDATE_POOL. The help text says the default is 'COGNIMEM_CANDIDATE_POOL or min(200, max(100, 4×limit))'. A user setting COGNIMEM_CANDIDATE_POOL to tune these modes gets no effect and no warning, and reports built on the help text state the wrong pool.
unverified.fix: Update the help text to say the env/100-floor default applies only to reranked (hybrid) search, and that fusion-only search uses max(20, 4×limit). Optionally warn when COGNIMEM_CANDIDATE_POOL is set but the search is not reranked.

unverified.title: _ROMAN_I removes the real pronoun after a sentence-initial adverb followed by a comma, so the disclosure is dropped after 1 hour
unverified.scenario: The second alternative, \b[A-Z][a-z]+\s+I(?=\s*[.,;:!?)]|$), matches any capitalised word followed by 'I' and a comma. That covers discourse markers at the start of a sentence. Probe results (all user role): 'Honestly I, uh, moved to Berlin.', 'So I, um, got engaged to Priya.', 'Well I, for one, grew up in Ohio.', 'Unfortunately I, lost the job at Acme.' and 'Mostly I, work nights at the hospital.' all give self_disclosure()=False, then TEMPORARY/working with a 1-hour expiry. The new feature is meant to keep exactly these statements, and here they are silently lost.
unverified.fix: Drop ',' and ';' from the lookahead (a regnal or ordinal 'I' is almost always followed by '.', ')', '?', '!' or the end of the string). Also skip matches where the capitalised word starts the sentence (preceded by ^ or [.!?]\s+), or require the preceding word to be a proper noun that is not a common adverb. Add the cases above as positive self_disclosure tests.

unverified.title: First-person text the user pastes for editing or translation, and instructional 'we', are now kept for 90 days as the user's own events
unverified.scenario: self_disclosure() only strips double-quoted text and inverted or reaction phrases, so any remaining \b(i|we)\b counts as a disclosure. 'Translate: I was born in a small town in Ohio' and 'We can compute the derivative by the chain rule' were TEMPORARY (1 hour) before this change. Now they are EPISODIC/short_term kept for 90 days, and retrieval/generation can surface 'I was born in a small town in Ohio' as a fact about the user.
unverified.fix: Treat text after an imperative editing or translation prefix (^(?:translate|rewrite|proofread|fix|correct|paraphrase|summari[sz]e|edit)\b[^:]*:) the same way as quoted speech and remove it before the pronoun check. Count 'we' only when it is followed by a past-tense or possession verb (we went/moved/have/bought...), not by modals (we can/could/should/will).

unverified.title: locomo_ann step ignores --structure, so exact and ANN LoCoMo arms run different pipelines
unverified.scenario: The locomo step appends --structure when it is not 'default', but the locomo_ann command does not. With `--structure none --ann-arms` (the e2-style attribution run), exact LoCoMo runs with no structured reordering while ANN LoCoMo runs with the default steps. The exact-vs-ANN comparison then mixes two changes, and the ANN snapshot is labelled with the wrong structure.
unverified.fix: Build the locomo_ann command from the same argument list as locomo (including --structure) and append only --ann and --output.

unverified.title: LoCoMo headline metrics include the adversarial category-5 questions
unverified.scenario: locomo.run puts all categories into 'metrics' (1973 questions, 446 of them category 5) and computes 'answerable_metrics' separately. report.collect, SUMMARY.md and report_delta read 'metrics', contrary to the locomo.py docstring that category 5 is 'reported separately'. In e4, hybrid_reranked Recall@5 is 0.668 including category 5 and 0.681 excluding it, so the headline is not comparable with standard LoCoMo retrieval numbers.
unverified.fix: Use report['answerable_metrics'] for the headline sections in report.collect, and add the adversarial set as its own section.

unverified.title: Pool metrics are cut at 100 when candidate_limit is above 100
unverified.scenario: run_query calls search with limit=min(pool, 100) because search caps limit at 100, then computes pool_metrics on those returned hits. With --candidate-limit 101-200 the reranker sees up to 200 candidates, but pool_hit and pool_recall see only the top 100 after reranking. Pool hit is understated and reranker_recovery is overstated. locomo.py:144/151 has the same issue.
unverified.fix: Take the pool membership from search diagnostics (the full fused id list) rather than from the truncated hits, or reject candidate_limit > 100 in the harness.
